title: ACES: Who Tests the Tests? Leave-One-Out AUC Consistency for Code Generation
summary: Selecting LLM-generated code candidates using LLM-generated tests is challenging because the tests themselves may be incorrect. Existing methods either treat all tests equally or rely on ad-hoc heuristics to filter unreliable tests. Yet determining test correctness requires knowing which codes are correct, creating a circular dependency. Our key insight is that we need not determine test correctness at all: test votes should rank, not merely count. What matters is not how many codes pass a test,…
description: LLM-generated code, test correctness, circular dependency, leave-one-out evaluation, LOO-AUC
developer_name: Hui Sun, Yun-Ji Zhang, Zheng Xie, Ren-Biao Liu, Yali Du et al. (7 authors)

analysis.detail_brief: Selecting LLM-generated code candidates using LLM-generated tests is challenging because the tests themselves may be incorrect. Existing methods either treat all tests equally or rely on ad-hoc heuristics to filter unreliable tests. Yet determining test correctness requires knowing which codes are correct, creating a circular dependency. Our key insight is that we need not determine test correctness at all: test votes should rank, not merely count.
